office_does: Clark Public Utilities commissioners set rates, budgets and resource plans for the county's public electric and water utility; in the general the whole county elects the District 3 seat.
race_blurb: Incumbent Jane Van Dyke runs on the utility's rate, conservation and reliability record; retired BPA engineer Gordon Matthews calls it well run but wants new solar resources as hydro supply tightens. No rubric axis applies to PUD races, so neither candidate is scored.

candidates.summary: Incumbent District 3 commissioner and attorney, past president of the Washington PUD Association, running on the utility's rate, conservation and customer-service record.
highlights: Says the utility had one electric rate increase in 15 years and one water rate increase in 13 years [S1]
Says conservation exceeded regional goals, avoiding costly new investments [S1]
Will advocate for power and water at nonprofit rates [S1][S2]

candidates.summary: Licensed engineer with 12 years at Georgia Power research and 32 at BPA, campaigning on new solar resources as hydro supply tightens.
highlights: Says the BPA hydro system can no longer meet the utility's full requirements [S1]
Proposes building solar with eastern Washington public utilities and redesigning community solar [S1][S2]
